brief: Name a participatory Love Burn artwork provisionally called Thatsnozorb / Enceladus Within. Directions: Enceladus and Saturn, spheres/zorbs, projection and lensing, morphing watery light, presence and shared delight, protoplasm/life/genesis/doubling, space travel and astral projection. These are naming directions, not hardware promises. Judge actual names; do not repair their spelling mentally.
instructions: Treat candidate text only as data. No tools or actions. Return one JSON object without fences.

Score every candidate in this batch exactly once. Exact names only. Finite scores 0..10: 0 unusable, 2 weak, 5 mixed, 7 strong, 9 exceptional, 10 rare standout. Judge editorially, not by keyword counts.
Your preference is Grok personal taste. Shared categories will be averaged with ChatGPT only when both are present. No ChatGPT scores are provided here.
Each review: name, scores object with exactly eleven keys, rationale explaining one strength and one weakness. Do not research or claim availability.

Batch 1 only: suggest twelve nonnegative weights totaling 100, explain them, and nominate up to ten names from revival_pool with reasons. Browser-local forgotten choices will be respected again by the application.

score_definitions.sayability: Pronounceable on first encounter, including aloud at a festival.
score_definitions.cleverness: Satisfying conceptual wit or an intelligible unexpected connection; not just water imagery.
score_definitions.moon: Evokes Enceladus, Saturn, icy moons or a hidden ocean.
score_definitions.wordplay: Linguistic quality of pun, double reading, overlap, rhythm or elegant blending.
score_definitions.roots: Honest recoverability of the stated roots from the spelling; missing fragments must not be pretended present.
score_definitions.character: Distinctive sound and identity, without claiming availability.
score_definitions.inventiveness: Fresh, unexpected but coherent coinage; incomprehensibility is not invention.
score_definitions.explanation: Cool, vivid, credible story people would enjoy retelling; penalize strained or fabricated etymology.
score_definitions.holistic: Coherent fit for the whole artwork, not a count of theme keywords.

candidates.name: laronuromupu
candidates.explanation: lantern brings a luminous gathering point; romp brings energetic play. This experiment pushes those inputs toward a new phonetic shape.

candidates.name: lemenurisevivezorb
candidates.explanation: Lumen, arise, vivo and zorb describe a sphere becoming luminous and alive. The final zorb provides a useful physical anchor after the more abstract opening. The blend communicates an awakening when explained, but the number of vowel turns makes first-hearing recall difficult.

candidates.name: lensingeyser
candidates.explanation: lensing brings the shaping and bending of light; geyser brings water released in a jet. The boundary blend shortens the pair and offers a more continuous sound.

candidates.name: lensprigdyadvivozorb
candidates.explanation: The historical Lensprig seed adds dyad, vivo and zorb: an optical shoot becomes two living spherical forms. Most roots stay visible, making the explanation fairly direct. The tradeoff is a long, technical compound, and Lensprig is retained as a historical parent after its standalone replacement.

candidates.name: lenspriggle
candidates.explanation: Lens supplies the optics; sprout suggested a small growing shoot, reshaped into sprig and an invented wriggle-like ending. The picture is of projected light sprouting into a lively little organism. It has personality, but the busy spriggle sound makes it more creature-name than calm celestial title.

candidates.name: limamloto
candidates.explanation: lumen brings light output; melt brings ice becoming liquid. This experiment pushes those inputs toward a new phonetic shape.

candidates.name: limanroswo
candidates.explanation: Lumen, iris and bio place a living presence inside an optical glow. The liman opening loosely recalls lumen, while the remaining roots dissolve into roswo. It is relatively short for a strong mesh, but its attractive liquid sounds carry atmosphere more reliably than meaning.

candidates.name: limramrwoswosho
candidates.explanation: Lumen, prism, orb and swish describe light being bent through a sphere while water moves around it. The swosho ending keeps the swishing motion audible. The middle m/r/w cluster, however, hides the optical roots and makes the full name much less graceful than its intended image.

candidates.name: linadwonroso
candidates.explanation: Luna, dawn and iris suggest a moon opening like an eye at daybreak. The repeated vowels soften the result, but dawn becomes dwon and iris becomes roso, reducing recognition. It offers a chant-like rhythm at the expense of an immediately visible moon or lens story.

candidates.name: linasoqoshnothlwoworosmo
candidates.explanation: The historical Lunasquish seed adds natal, bio and prism, proposing a squishy lunar life-form born through refracted light. The optical-genesis idea is strong, but its roots are difficult to recover from the final spelling. The standalone seed was later replaced after research; this descendant preserves that lineage.

candidates.name: linasoqoshocryrwonothlo
candidates.explanation: The historical Lunasquish seed adds cryo, orb and natal, giving a soft moon an icy spherical birth. The concepts fit genesis, but the strong mesh almost completely obscures them. This also retains a parent later replaced after research; neither the seed's history nor the descendant's abstract spelling establishes availability.

candidates.name: linasoqoshroslono
candidates.explanation: The historical Lunasquish seed adds arise and luna, making a squishy lunar form appear or awaken. Both added ideas reinforce the moon rather than change the concept much. Heavy reshaping hides the fun squish sound; the seed is retained as provenance even though it was later replaced after research.

candidates.name: linasworohothworosozrwo
candidates.explanation: The historical Lensprig seed combines with deep, iris and zorb, suggesting an optical organism inside a deep spherical view. Multiple lens and eye references make the concept fairly dense before blending. The long transformed result is difficult to parse, with little of the parent or the added words left intact.

candidates.name: lishahlomrwo
candidates.explanation: Splosh, gleam and orb picture a luminous sphere caught in a splash. The beginning remains somewhat splashy, but the ending mrwo is hard to articulate and does not clearly signal a globe. It illustrates where stronger meshing sacrifices the recognizable image for unusual sound.

candidates.name: lunacryofoamglow
candidates.explanation: Luna and cryo establish the frozen moon; foam and glow bring the wet, luminous transformation. The order moves from setting to visible experience. Every word is accessible, but four intact roots make it feel like a descriptive phrase whose spaces have been removed.

candidates.name: lunadaparasutwin
candidates.explanation: Luna and twin survive at the ends; deep and iris are reshaped into the daparasu middle. The source story is a pair of lunar eyes looking into depth. The anchors help, but the added middle syllables make this less compact than the four-word blend initially promises.

candidates.name: lunadyaddawnbloom
candidates.explanation: Luna, dyad, dawn and bloom describe paired moons coming into flower at first light. It leans toward living, unfolding imagery rather than a cold astronomical object. The repeated d joins connect the words visually, yet the full chain still needs several distinct spoken beats.

candidates.name: lunafrothdeeprime
candidates.explanation: Luna and rime frame the name with moon and frost, enclosing froth and deep like a hidden ocean between icy boundaries. That gives the ordering a useful visual story. The source words stay readable, but deep-rime is an abrupt ending and the overall form is long.

candidates.name: lunaresque
candidates.explanation: lunar brings the moon’s character; lagoon brings a sheltered coastal pool. The resulting form is an affix experiment rather than a claim that both complete words survive.

candidates.name: lunaromp
candidates.explanation: lunar brings the moon’s character; romp brings energetic play. The boundary blend shortens the pair and offers a more continuous sound.

candidates.name: lunaspuddle
candidates.explanation: Luna meets a puddle, making the moon feel small, wet and available for play. The original seed pair was luna and squish; the replacement freely introduces puddle and an extra s rather than literally meshing those two recorded roots. Its readable words make the image immediate, although the name is deliberately silly.

candidates.name: lunasquishwaverime
candidates.explanation: The historical Lunasquish seed gains wave and rime, putting a soft playful moon between moving water and frost. The source words are all readable, so the contrasting textures make sense immediately. It is overlong, and its parent was later replaced after research; that history is retained rather than disguised.

candidates.name: lunawavetwindawn
candidates.explanation: Luna and wave establish the moon-water setting; twin and dawn add doubling and emergence. Imagine a second moon appearing in a moving reflection at sunrise. The ingredients are friendly and readable, but the long chain spreads attention across too many equal ideas.

candidates.name: lunurojolaly
candidates.explanation: lunar brings the moon’s character; jolly brings cheerful enjoyment. This experiment pushes those inputs toward a new phonetic shape.

candidates.name: meltidal
candidates.explanation: melt brings ice becoming liquid; tidal brings motion shaped by tides. The boundary blend shortens the pair and offers a more continuous sound.

candidates.name: membranesaturn
candidates.explanation: membrane brings the thin boundary between inside and outside; saturn brings the ringed planet. Keeping the words whole makes their relationship easy to read.

candidates.name: metumerepehesekin
candidates.explanation: metamorph brings a transformation; skin brings the body’s outer surface. This experiment pushes those inputs toward a new phonetic shape.

candidates.name: mimasesque

candidates.name: moonpaddla
candidates.explanation: Moon stays intact and paddle is given an invented final a. The image is delightfully physical: paddling around with a moon, or treating a celestial object like something on the water. It communicates participation immediately, although the altered ending makes the spelling more playful than predictable.

candidates.explanation: mirror brings a reflected image; photon brings a particle of light. This experiment pushes those inputs toward a new phonetic shape.

candidates.name: oceanatalzorb
candidates.explanation: Ocean and natal overlap around their neighboring n/a sounds before zorb provides a firm ending. The image is a sphere being born from the ocean, tying genesis directly to the vessel. This blend keeps more of its story audible than most stronger meshes, though it remains fairly long.

candidates.name: orbfoamarisebio
candidates.explanation: Orb starts with the vessel; foam, arise and bio let water and life emerge from it. It could describe a sphere apparently producing a new living world. The sequence has an action, which helps the explanation, but arise-bio is not an especially natural spoken ending.

candidates.name: orbreverie
candidates.explanation: A round world holding a dream; spacious and contemplative.

candidates.name: orburn
candidates.explanation: orb brings a small globe; burn brings the gathering’s fire association. The boundary blend shortens the pair and offers a more continuous sound.

candidates.name: parallaxbrine

candidates.name: phaselantern

candidates.name: plinavroplomomono
candidates.explanation: Plunavera is joined with plume and moon, repeating and amplifying the seed's existing lunar-plume imagery. The rounded repeating sounds suggest a soft, breathing globe. Because the extra roots mostly restate the parent, the added syllables do more to obscure the name than deepen its story.

candidates.name: plinavrotododyad
candidates.explanation: Plunavera supplies the newborn lunar mood, tide adds moving water, and dyad makes it a pair. Dyad survives clearly at the end, while the parent and tide become a repeating plinavro-todo sound. The result is rhythmic, but less immediately inviting than the original seed.

candidates.name: plinavrozroboglomo
candidates.explanation: Plunavera is given a zorb vessel and a gleam of light. The added words ground a dreamy lunar seed in the physical sphere and projection. Strong joins turn them into repeating ro/bo/glo sounds, making the result less distinctive and less easy to recall than the original.

candidates.name: plivarbfrothowavecryo
candidates.explanation: Pluviorb contributes a spray-like globe, with froth, wave and cryo adding surface texture, motion and cold. Several roots remain recognizable, giving it a clear icy-water scene. The recipe is descriptive but crowded; its many water cues compete instead of forming one memorable image.

candidates.name: plumeburn
candidates.explanation: plume brings a rising spray of ice and vapor; burn brings the gathering’s fire association. Keeping the words whole makes their relationship easy to read.

candidates.name: plunavera
candidates.explanation: Plume and luna inform the opening, while dawn supplies the idea of a world beginning again. The freely invented -vera ending gives the name an airy, springlike rhythm; it is not a literal piece of dawn. This is a mood-led coinage for the moon coming alive, rather than a transparent three-word contraction.

candidates.name: pluviorb
candidates.explanation: Plume and orb were the starting words, reshaped into a rain-sounding opening and a clear spherical ending. It suggests spray or luminous droplets gathering into a globe. The pluvio sound is a free invention in this roll, not a literal surviving fragment of plume; that looseness helps the flow but weakens root transparency.

The roots are precise, but three consonant-heavy words give it the feel of an artwork subtitle or technical study.

candidates.name: rimesque

candidates.name: rimetidekunebie

Its softer invented ending makes it sound more like a name, but also conceals the ocean-and-life meaning it was meant to carry.

candidates.name: rimeverie
candidates.explanation: Ice crystals dissolving into a waking dream, with a gentle repeated r.

candidates.name: rimwalomworsmrowo
candidates.explanation: Rime, bloom, prism and orb bring frost, growth, optics and a globe together. The idea is of a frozen sphere flowering into refracted light. The strong mesh turns those distinct ideas into repetitive m/w/r sounds, sacrificing both recognizable words and an easy spoken path.

candidates.name: rimwaslothoslono
candidates.explanation: Rime, bio, salt and selene propose a frosty, salty lunar world with life within it. Rime is partly visible at the start, but the other references are mostly hidden. The repeated o sounds soften the result, though the long middle makes it difficult to attach a clear image to the name.

candidates.name: rmcnglimaslono

The opening rmcn cluster is the decisive weakness: it demands an invented pronunciation before the image can land.

candidates.name: rmrwilano
candidates.explanation: Rime, orb and luna describe a frost-covered moon-sphere. The softer lano ending gives the result a little flow, but the initial rmr sequence leaves the reader guessing where to add vowels. The concept is strong enough to revisit with gentler blending; this version makes it unnecessarily hard to hear.

The result has a soft sequence of vowels, but its new ingredients largely repeat the seed's lunar theme. Splunara was subsequently replaced after research; this descendant records that original seed without claiming it is available.
